tool_arguments.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Fresh standalone second phase of a small grooming gesture for the exact adopted Florida Panther. INPUT1 is adopted neutral: sole identity, style, proportions, palette, face/eye and standing-body reference. INPUT2 is a candidate phaseA: use ONLY for which original arm is moving and its gesture continuity, not a new identity or body redesign. Draw one complete same character on genuinely transparent1254square canvas with the original neutral standing head/torso/feet size and position. Keep one right-side long tail with dark tip, same3whiskers per cheek, cream muzzle/chest/belly, tan paper texture and warm brown contours. Same plain white eyes+brown pupils WITHOUT highlights, same closed curved smile. The moving paw is on VIEWER LEFT, the SAME paw as input2. The VIEWER-LEFT forepaw now gently touches the VIEWER-LEFT cheek and begins a tiny outward grooming stroke; viewer-right arm remains DOWN exactly as neutral. Do not switch paws. Keep a single clean paw/face overlap, no duplicated hand or detached strokes. Feet remain planted. No human fingers/thumb, new pale pads, extra limbs, mirrored tail, text, ray effects, sparkles, objects, ground or shadow. No mouth opening or tongue. Crisp native contour, clean intentional soft painted paper, no muddy patches or bleeding. Preserve whole standing torso length and head level; do not squash to fit.
